title: Autopsy and Inheritance
premise: Noor Brightwater, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has catalogued every death recorded in its crypt for thirty years — so when a stranger is found dead in the locked crypt wearing clothes cut from Noor's own wardrobe, the police assume she's either victim or killer. The dead man, it emerges, was the last living witness to the 'closed' case of a chorister's disappearance two decades ago, and someone inside the cathedral close is silencing the past. As Noor digs through ledgers, confessions, and her late mother's letters, she discovers the original investigation buried the truth to protect the cathedral's beloved dean — and that the current killings are an inheritance of guilt passed down like the vestments themselves. In the end Noor must choose between exposing the institution that gave her belonging and letting an innocent man hang for it; she chooses truth, forcing a public reckoning that costs her the archive but finally gives the dead their names back.
about_author: Coral Underhill spent a decade as a parish records volunteer in northern England before turning to crime fiction, where her love of dusty registers and unreliable memory shows on every page. She writes from a converted vestry and claims she can smell a lie in a ledger.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Establishes her ordered life among the cathedral archives and her ritual of locking the crypt each night. She notices one ledger page slightly askew — a small wrongness that unsettles her more than it should. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Stranger in My Clothes
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A body is found in the sealed crypt dressed in garments copied from Noor's own closet, down to a mended cuff. Police treat her as suspect. Emotional beat: violation and vertigo — her identity literally worn by a corpse.

chapters.title: Detective Ferro
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Noor and Detective Ferro, who suspects but also studies her. Ferro reveals the crypt lock was never forced. Noor realizes only three people hold keys. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming under suspicion.

chapters.title: The Case Everyone Closed
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She identifies the dead man: Thomas Reeve, once a choirboy witness in the 1999 disappearance of chorister Elsie Marsh — a case ruled accidental and sealed. Emotional beat: dread of reopening what the institution buried.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Archival digging shows Elsie's file pages excised with archival precision — someone with training. Suspicion falls on the cathedral staff. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Dean's Warm Welcome
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Dean Ambrose Vellacott, charismatic guardian of the cathedral, gently warns Noor against 'wounding the living for the sake of the dead.' Emotional beat: seductive pressure to belong over truth.

chapters.title: What Thomas Knew
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Autopsy shows Reeve was poisoned weeks before death and kept somewhere — he died elsewhere and was moved. The staging in Noor's clothes was deliberate framing. Emotional beat: cold calculation behind the mystery.

chapters.title: Mother's Letters
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Among her late mother's effects Noor finds letters hinting her mother worked at the cathedral in 1999 and feared something. Emotional beat: personal stakes deepen; grief reopened.

chapters.title: The Second Keyholder
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Sacristan Peter Oakes, keyholder number two, is found unconscious, his quarters ransacked — someone searching for something specific. Emotional beat: escalating danger to anyone connected.

chapters.title: Elsie's Ghost
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Reinterviews reveal Elsie was last seen entering the crypt with an adult whose face no witness will name. The town's silence is complicity. Emotional beat: collective guilt as antagonist.

chapters.title: An Offer of Belonging
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Vellacott offers Noor a permanent endowed post and hints he knows about her mother. Acceptance would mean silence. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth made explicit and tempting.

chapters.title: The Vestment Inheritance
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor traces the copied clothes to a set of vestments altered by the same seamstress who made her mother's coat — linking the frame directly to 1999. Emotional beat: the past stitched into the present.

chapters.title: Peter Wakes
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A groggy Oakes whispers a name — 'the organ loft' — before recanting in terror. Ferro suspects witness tampering. Emotional beat: fear outlasting memory.

chapters.title: Choir Practice
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She attends evensong and watches the choir master, Ivo Renwick, conduct; his eyes keep finding hers. A hymnal holds a pressed flower like ones in Elsie's memorial photos. Emotional beat: menace hidden in beauty.

chapters.title: The File That Wasn't Burned
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. A retired constable admits the 1999 inquiry was steered from above; evidence exists in a private safe. Before he can say whose, he dies of 'heart failure.' Emotional beat: justice outside the law begins to look necessary.

chapters.title: Breaking the Seal
chapters.summary: Noir-tinged Noor POV. Noor breaks into the restricted muniment room at night using her archivist's knowledge, finding a photograph of Elsie alive after her supposed death date. Emotional beat: everything the official story rests on collapses.

chapters.title: Alive After All
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. If Elsie lived, what did Reeve actually witness? Noor reconstructs a timeline showing Reeve was blackmailing someone for twenty years. Emotional beat: motive emerging from the dust.

chapters.title: Vellacott's Sermon
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Vellacott preaches publicly on forgiveness and moving on, clearly aimed at Noor; the congregation's eyes turn on her. Emotional beat: isolation — the community closing ranks.

chapters.title: Ferro's Doubt
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Ferro's superiors order him to close the case as burglary gone wrong. He keeps working off-book, trusting Noor against procedure. Emotional beat: the law failing; two outsiders bound together.

chapters.title: The Seamstress Confesses
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The elderly seamstress admits she copied Noor's clothes under duress years ago for 'a memorial garment' — commissioned by someone she'll only name in person. Emotional beat: pity and fear entangled.

chapters.title: Midnight Appointment
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor goes alone to meet the seamstress; finds her dead, staged like Reeve, wearing a scrap of Elsie's choir robe. A message: stop, or be dressed for your own funeral. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: My Mother's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Comparing documents, Noor recognizes her mother's handwriting on a 1999 receipt for children's shoes bought the week Elsie vanished. Her mother knew. Emotional beat: the ground of identity giving way.

chapters.title: What Noor Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Noor's POV. Memory surfaces: age nine, seeing her mother burn a box in the garden while crying, telling Noor never to ask about 'the girl.' Emotional beat: complicity inherited without consent.

chapters.title: Confronting the Archive of Self
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor nearly destroys her own findings to protect her mother's memory; Ferro talks her back from it. Emotional beat: the book's thematic crux — loyalty vs. truth turned inward.

chapters.title: The Organ Loft
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Searching the organ loft, they find a hidden cache: Elsie's diary, proving she discovered financial fraud in the cathedral restoration fund and was smuggled away, not murdered — but by whom, and where is she now? Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Renwick Breaks
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Cornered, choir master Renwick confesses he helped spirit Elsie away on orders from above, believing he protected her; he names the voice on the phone as Vellacott's. Emotional beat: a small man's lifetime of cowardice spilling out.

chapters.title: Vellacott Vanishes
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The dean disappears; his office contains a forged letter implicating Noor's mother in Elsie's murder. The trap closes: expose the truth and damn her mother, or stay silent and let the frame stand. Emotional beat: the cruelest choice yet.

chapters.title: Reading the Forgeries
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Using forensic archival skill, Noor proves the damning letter is written over a palimpsest of Vellacott's own drafts — he authored the frame against her mother long ago. Emotional beat: expertise as weapon; fury as fuel.

chapters.title: The Crypt Opens
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Following Vellacott's logic, Noor deduces his final destination: the walled-off sub-crypt where Elsie hid in 1999 — and where Vellacott kept the proof of his embezzlement ever since. Emotional beat: the building itself yielding its secret.

chapters.title: Below the Floor
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Alone, Noor descends into the sub-crypt and finds Elsie Marsh alive, elderly, hidden voluntarily for decades in exchange for silence — and finds Vellacott waiting there too. Emotional beat: claustrophobic confrontation with the whole truth.

chapters.title: The Dean's Confession
chapters.summary: Vellacott's monologue within Noor's POV. He explains the inheritance of sin: his mentor began the theft, he continued it, Reeve extorted him, and the murders were committed by his fixer — the sacristan's attacker, still loyal. Emotional beat: evil as respectable tradition.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Vellacott offers Noor everything: her mother cleared, her post endowed, Elsie protected — if the crypt stays sealed forever. Elsie herself begs Noor to accept. Emotional beat: even the victim asks for the lie.

chapters.title: The Witness Decides
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor refuses — not for justice abstractly, but because she watched her mother die carrying the secret. She triggers the emergency line, trading her sanctuary for truth. Emotional beat: costly, quiet courage.

chapters.title: Arrest in the Nave
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Off-book and risking his career, Ferro arrives with officers and arrests Vellacott and his fixer in front of morning congregation. Emotional beat: justice performed in public light at last.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The cathedral community reels; some thank Noor, most shun her. She is suspended from the archive pending review. Emotional beat: the loneliness of having been right.

chapters.title: Her Mother Cleared
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Evidence exonerates Noor's mother, who had only burned Vellacott's threats to protect young Noor. At the grave, Noor finally grieves cleanly. Emotional beat: reconciliation with the dead.

chapters.title: Elsie's Testimony
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Elsie, given immunity, testifies; the diocese dissolves its leadership. She thanks Noor not for rescue but for listening. Emotional beat: truth as a gift even when unwelcome.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The chapter offers Noor reinstatement if she signs a confidentiality agreement — the old bargain in new clothes. She declines. Emotional beat: refusing a smaller belonging for a larger integrity.

chapters.title: Requiem
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A memorial service for Elsie's lost years and for Reeve, the flawed blackmailer who nonetheless tried to make amends. Noor reads the names aloud from her own restored ledger. Emotional beat: mourning completed, names returned.

chapters.title: Autopsy and Inheritance
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, coda. Months later, Noor keeps a small independent records office by the cathedral gates; Ferro visits with cold coffee and a new unsolved case. She locks nothing anymore — except, at night, the door behind her. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt on chosen truth rather than inherited silence.
